assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalysed C-N coupling turned aryl amine synthesis from a forcing, substrate-limited problem into a routine, general transformation, via rationally designed ligands and a clear mechanistic picture. Its use in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis is ubiquitous and visible in countless later total and medicinal syntheses; this is the archetype of a method that changed how chemists build bonds.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the ligand-controlled, broadly general catalytic systems and mechanistic understanding that made the reaction practical. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work is a credited precursor but was not a general catalytic amination; two laureates is a clean configuration.
assessment.maturity: Over 25 years of independent confirmation and industrial scale use; recognition is, if anything, overdue, and the interpretation is stable.
uncertainties: Priority of the Kosugi (and possibly Migita) precedent versus the ligand-enabled general method is a historical judgment I cannot verify from the supplied text.
Cross-coupling was recognised in 2010, so the committee may see the topic as partly covered.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis opened a new mode of reactivity, single-electron radical generation under mild conditions, and enabled bond formations that were hard by two-electron chemistry. Adoption in discovery chemistry and industry is broad, and the concept is simple to apply, which I value.
assessment.attribution: MacMillan, Yoon and Stephenson published the foundational synthetic demonstrations in 2008-2009 and have driven the field; Nicewicz, Konig, Fukuzumi and Melchiorre are significant but the three-person limit forces exclusions. Ru/Ir photochemistry predates the work, so credit is somewhat entangled.
assessment.maturity: Mature in the sense of widespread uptake and replication across hundreds of groups; some applications are still evolving, but the core discovery is stable and timely.
uncertainties: MacMillan already shared the 2021 prize, which may weigh on the committee.
Allocation among the several early contributors is contestable and I have not verified exact priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Directed and ligand-controlled C-H functionalization lets chemists form bonds at otherwise inert positions, changing retrosynthetic thinking and shortening syntheses, which matches my emphasis on efficiency. Yu's ligand-accelerated, site-selective work is conceptually important and used in late-stage functionalization.
assessment.attribution: Yu (ligand and template control), Sanford (Pd/Pt-catalysed oxidative functionalization, mechanistic work) and Daugulis (early directing group approaches) are plausible leading contributors. Hartwig, Smith and others are credited in the entry, so the field is broad and attribution is diffuse.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly adopted but still developing; scope of general, predictable methods is not yet fully routine, so timing is somewhat early compared with older cross-coupling.
uncertainties: Field is large and attribution diffuse; any three-person subset is debatable.
Industrial adoption is less proven than for cross-coupling.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Isolation of stable carbenes overturned the view that such species were only transient, and N-heterocyclic carbenes became ubiquitous ligands and organocatalysts, including in metathesis catalysts. This is conceptually clear chemistry with large downstream impact.
assessment.attribution: Arduengo isolated the crystalline imidazol-2-ylidene (1991); Bertrand reported the earlier stable phosphinocarbene (1988) and later cyclic alkyl amino carbenes. Nolan, Rovis and Bode are more application-oriented contributors. Two laureates is a coherent configuration.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of confirmation and broad use; mature.
uncertainties: Priority between Bertrand's 1988 carbene and Arduengo's 1991 NHC may be contested.
Much of the downstream impact is tied to metathesis, already honoured in 2005.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom transfer radical polymerization gave a general, robust route to polymers with controlled molecular weight, architecture and functionality from ordinary monomers. It is widely practiced and has industrial uses, and is a real methodological advance in polymer synthesis.
assessment.attribution: Matyjaszewski and Sawamoto (with Kamigaito) reported the Cu and Ru-based systems in 1995; Wang worked with Matyjaszewski. Concurrent independent discovery makes the credit configuration reasonable at two but sensitive to who is excluded.
assessment.maturity: Mature, well replicated, and long in industrial use; timely.
uncertainties: Competing controlled radical methods (RAFT, nitroxide-mediated) could be seen as equally deserving, complicating a single recognition.
Kamigaito's role versus Sawamoto's is uncertain to me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Frustrated Lewis pairs showed that sterically encumbered acid/base pairs activate H2 and other small molecules without metals, a new concept that spawned metal-free hydrogenation and catalysis. It is chemically original and conceptually simple.
assessment.attribution: Stephan's 2006 discovery of metal-free H2 activation and Erker's subsequent contributions are the two natural credits, giving a tidy two-person prize.
assessment.maturity: About 20 years old and well confirmed, but practical impact on synthesis is still modest compared with transition-metal catalysis; recognition could be slightly early.
uncertainties: Practical adoption in synthesis and industry remains limited.
Welch/Stephan and Erker priority details I cannot verify.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Phosphoramidite chemistry made automated oligonucleotide synthesis routine and underpins primers, probes, sequencing, gene synthesis and nucleic acid therapeutics. It is a classic general synthetic method whose use is enormous and seen everywhere.
assessment.attribution: Caruthers developed the phosphoramidite method (1981) building on earlier phosphite triester work by Letsinger and Beaucage collaboration; Hood is credited for automation instruments, which is a weaker chemical contribution. A single-laureate configuration is defensible, but the supplied credit omits other contributors I would consider.
assessment.maturity: Foundational and decades-confirmed; recognition is overdue and unlikely to be premature.
uncertainties: Credit split between Caruthers, Beaucage and earlier phosphite chemistry is unresolved, and I cannot verify it.
Hood's role is instrumentation rather than chemistry.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native chemical ligation allows chemoselective joining of unprotected peptides, making total chemical synthesis and semisynthesis of proteins practical. It is an elegant, simple chemical idea with lasting influence in chemical biology and protein science.
assessment.attribution: Dawson, Muir, Kent (1994) introduced the method; Kent led its extension to total protein synthesis, with Muir for expressed protein ligation. Choosing two of Kent, Dawson and Muir for a prize is difficult; I propose Kent and Dawson as the core, with Muir a serious alternative.
assessment.maturity: Mature, broadly adopted for protein synthesis, though some applications are specialised; timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Exclusion of Muir (expressed protein ligation) or Danishefsky would be contentious.
Impact on mainstream chemistry is less ubiquitous than for synthetic methods in higher ranks.
